setup.zh: 坑底蜷着一只小银狐，伤得很重，只剩一条尾巴，尾根八处断口。它睁眼，龇牙。
setup.en: A little silver fox lies curled in the pit, badly hurt: one tail left, eight clean cuts at its root. It opens its eyes and bares its teeth.

recap.zh: 谷底的浅坑里，你救起一只伤重的小银狐——一条尾巴，尾根八处断口。
recap.en: In a pit on the valley floor you took up a badly hurt little silver fox — one tail, eight cuts at its root.

zh: 坑底一点银光，一明，一暗。
只剩一条尾巴。尾根上，八处断口。
en: A silver light in the pit, bright, then dim.
A little silver fox, fur like moonlit frost.
One tail left. At its root, eight clean cuts.

text.zh: 坑边的泥上没有一个脚印，也没有血拖过的痕迹——它倒像跟你一样，是从上头掉下来的。
text.en: No footprint in the mud at the rim, no trail of blood: it seems to have fallen from above, like you.

text.zh: 八处断口，一处比一处齐，不是野兽咬的，也不是夹子夹的——夹子夹不了这么齐。
text.en: Eight stumps, each cleaner than the last. Not a beast's bite, not a trap — no trap cuts so clean.

story.zh:
他没有走过去，先蹲在一棵银叶树后面看了很久。坑边没有脚印，没有血迹拖过的痕迹，四下里也没有别的动静。他捡起一根枯枝扔到坑边，那光还是一明一暗，并不理会。他这才一点一点地挪了过去。

坑里是一只[狐狸]{注=yinyue-fox}。很小，比吴婆婆家那只猫还小一圈——吴婆婆家那只猫胖得像个枕头，这只狐狸大概只有半个枕头。

它蜷在坑底的泥水里，一身的毛是银色的，不是灰，是真正的银，像月光冻成了一层霜铺在它身上，雨水落上去，不沾也不湿，就那么滑了下去。可它伤得很重，一条后腿歪着，身上好几道口子，血把银毛染成了暗红。

它身后只有一条尾巴，尾巴根上还有好几处断口，整整齐齐，像给什么极快、极利的东西一刀一刀斩断的。小满数了数，共是八处。

他愣住了，把怀里吴婆婆的木牌摸了出来，就着那一点银光，一条一条地数木牌上那只蜷着的小狐狸的尾巴，数来数去，是九条。

便在这时，坑里的狐狸睁开了眼睛。那是一双金色的眼睛，瞳仁竖着，冷得像冬天的井水。它看着他，龇了一下牙，喉咙里发出一声又小又凶的呜咽，可它连头都抬不起来。

他爹说过，受伤的野兽最凶，碰都别去碰。
story.en:
He didn't go over. First he crouched behind a silver-leafed tree and watched for a long time. There were no footprints around the hollow, no marks of anything bleeding being dragged, and nothing else stirring anywhere. He picked up a dead branch and threw it to the edge of the hollow. The light went on glowing and dimming and paid it no attention. Only then did he edge over, a little at a time.

In the hollow lay a [fox]{注=yinyue-fox}. A very small one, a size smaller than Granny Wu's cat — Granny Wu's cat was as fat as a pillow; this fox was maybe half a pillow.

It was curled in the muddy water at the bottom of the hollow, and its fur was silver. Not grey: true silver, like moonlight frozen into a layer of frost and laid over it. Rain that landed on it neither clung nor soaked in; it just slid off. But it was badly hurt. One hind leg was twisted, there were several gashes on its body, and blood had stained the silver fur dark red.

Behind it there was only one tail, and at the root of that tail were several stumps, cut clean and even, as if something very fast and very sharp had cut them off, one stroke after another. Xiaoman counted. Eight in all.

He froze. He took Granny Wu's tablet out of his jacket and, by that little bit of silver light, counted the tails of the little curled-up fox on it, one by one. He counted them again and again. Nine.

Just then the fox in the hollow opened its eyes. They were golden eyes, with slit pupils, cold as well water in winter. It looked at him and bared its teeth, and a small, fierce whimper came from its throat. But it couldn't even lift its head.

His father had said a wounded animal is the fiercest kind; don't so much as touch it.

label.en: Take off your jacket and wrap it up

exits.means: saves the fox, picks it up, wraps it in the jacket, helps it

goal.zh: 受伤的野兽最凶。别打它——挡住它咬，站住三个回合。
goal.en: A hurt animal is the fiercest. Don't strike it — take its bites, and stand three of its turns.

game._foe: 第一回's teaching fight (2026-10-22, Hanli: 「关键是能留住玩家」 — the card fight met before 第三回's 蠪侄): the book's own face-off, 「受伤的野兽最凶，碰都别去碰」, then the coat, the bite, 「它不咬了」 (this exit's passage, unchanged). A 试 of nerve like the 三试: stand three of its turns. Three cards the book gives him here — 枯枝 (「他捡起一根枯枝扔到坑边」: play a card that strikes), 补丁外衣 (the coat over it: a body that takes the bite), 不怕 (「不怕。我也掉下来了」) — and 结束回合. No 反噬 (`foe.fatigue: false`, 2026-10-22: a tutorial teaches no penalty) — his five cards are all in hand, so his deck is dry from the first draw. It cannot be lost (it bites for 1–2; he stands 20); 认输 or a loss is 「再来」 (retry). No loot, no card, nothing paid.

withdrawn.zh: 它缩在坑底，喉咙里还在呜咽。
withdrawn.en: It curls at the bottom of the pit, still whimpering.

story.zh:
小满看了它很久，心想：它要是死在这儿，就什么都不是了；它要是活下来——不知道它会是什么。可他知道，一只尾巴给人一刀一刀斩掉的东西，和一个给人一把推到灶台边上的孩子，差不太多。

他脱下了外衣。那是他娘去年冬天拿他爹的旧袄改的，袖口打着补丁，补丁上还打着补丁。他用枯枝挑着，轻轻盖在它身上，再隔着衣裳把它抱了起来。它还是咬了他一口，隔着两层布，咬在他虎口上，不深，可是很疼。

他「嘶」了一声，却没有松手，说道：「不怕。我也掉下来了。咱俩，做个伴。」

它不咬了。它在他的衣裳里抖了一下，然后把脸埋进了那块补丁里。
story.en:
Xiaoman looked at it for a long time and thought: if it dies here, it won't be anything at all. If it lives — who knows what it'll be. But he did know that something whose tails had been cut off one stroke at a time, and a child who'd been shoved against a stove, weren't so very different.

He took off his jacket. His mother had made it last winter out of his father's old padded coat; there were patches on the cuffs, and patches on the patches. He lifted it on a dead branch, laid it gently over the fox, and then picked it up, wrapped in the jacket. It bit him anyway, through two layers of cloth, in the web of his thumb. Not deep, but it hurt.

He hissed, but he didn't let go. "Don't be scared. I fell down here too. We'll keep each other company."

It stopped biting. It shivered once inside his jacket, and then it buried its face in a patch.

exits.means: leaves the fox alone, backs away, walks off

story.zh:
小满往后退了一步，又一步。坑里那点银光，一明，一暗，一明——暗下去的那一下，比刚才长。

他停住了。他想起那八道断口，整整齐齐的，一刀一刀；又想起灶台，想起那只在半空里翻了两个筋斗的碗。他的脚，便再也迈不动了。
story.en:
Xiaoman took a step back, then another. The silver light in the hollow went bright, dim, bright — and the dim lasted longer than before.

He stopped. He thought of those eight stumps, clean and even, one stroke at a time; and of the stove, and the bowl that turned two somersaults in the air. And his feet wouldn't carry him another step.
